rubrics.date: The Vigil is the Wednesday before the Ascension (Rubricae generales 28, 31). When one of the two named second-class feasts takes its place, the Vigil is commemorated rather than transferred. A Vigil occurring on a Sunday or a first-class feast is omitted entirely (33).
rubrics.scope: Mass only, through the Collect, Secret and Postcommunion of the actual Vigil formulary. The calendar resolves each slot to that formulary; the reused Fifth Sunday after Easter bodies do not change the commemoration's identity into a Sunday.
rubrics.rank: An ordinary commemoration: the second-class Vigil is not among the privileged commemorations listed in Rubricae generales 109. It is made in low Mass and conventual Mass, but not in a sung Mass that is not conventual (108, 111 a).
rubrics.admission: The named second-class feasts have precedence over the second-class Vigil (Rubricae generales 91, places 16 and 21). The day admits one commemoration (111 c, 434); the Vigil, as de Tempore, takes that place before another ordinary commemoration (113–114). Thus on 31 May it excludes the commemoration of Saint Petronilla. No ordinary commemoration is admitted in a non-conventual sung Mass (111 a).
rubrics.conclusion: For the Mass oration followed by this single commemoration, each has its own conclusion (Rubricae generales 436–437). At the Secret, the Mass oration and its conclusion are said quietly; only the final Secret's concluding Per omnia saecula saeculorum and the response Amen are audible (480–481). This does not prescribe a separate conclusion for every intermediate oration when more prayers are present.
